research_stage: portfolio construction audit, not signal discovery
research_question: Do the NSI Q5 (heavy net-share-issuance) and Quality Q5 (lowest composite quality) hard exclusions, applied to the live V3.1 composite specification, independently and jointly improve the finished portfolio's risk-adjusted returns -- and if so, by how much?
background: Prior signal-level research found NSI Q5 (long-short t=5.26) and Quality Q5 (long-short t=4.39) carry real information, with both spreads driven almost entirely by the short leg (long leg near-zero alpha). A separate exclusion-filter test (Portfolio D in that prior work) showed active alpha t=5.38 vs. an equal-weight benchmark, but that was subsequently identified as factor tilting relative to the benchmark, not genuine alpha vs SPY. V3.1 already applies both exclusions as guardrails; their marginal contribution to the finished, IBS-dominated composite has never been isolated. Framing: a filter that reduces max drawdown while preserving CAGR is valuable for its own sake (it creates room for more aggressive sizing elsewhere), independent of whether it shows measurable factor alpha.

base_portfolio_spec.source: paper_trading/config.json tracks.composite_v3_1, as running in paper trading (Track 3)
base_portfolio_spec.signals: IBS (earnings-conditioned, 5-day trailing average, percentile-ranked, earnings-day names forced to neutral 0.50), RSI2 (100-RSI(close,2), percentile-ranked), Sector RS (63-day return, percentile-ranked within Fama sector, NaN sector filled to 0.5), Turnaround Tuesday (binary: 1 if that Friday's own daily return < -1%, else 0)
base_portfolio_spec.universe: Full Sharadar PIT-eligible common stocks (NASDAQ/NYSE/NYSEMKT/NYSEARCA/BATS), excluding Fama sectors Financial Services, Real Estate, Healthcare; price >= $1; trailing 63-day median dollar volume >= $500,000; >= 252 days price history
base_portfolio_spec.rebalance: Friday close signal, Monday-open execution (next trading day's open after signal date for entry and for exit)
base_portfolio_spec.selection_and_weighting: Top quintile of composite score among eligible (post-exclusion) names, equal weight
base_portfolio_spec.cost_model: 10bps round-trip, applied to weekly symmetric-difference turnover: cost_week = turnover_week * 0.0010, annualized as cost_week * 52
base_portfolio_spec.note_on_weight_provenance: config.json flags these weights as differing from an IC-based re-optimization computed in a prior session (IBS=0.92/RSI2=0/SectorRS=0/Tue=0.08, no earnings conditioning). This audit uses the LIVE spec (.62/.22/.10/.06, earnings-conditioned) as registered, unchanged -- re-optimizing weights is out of scope for this audit.

stripped_base_construction.definition: Identical signals, weights, universe, rebalance cadence, cost model, and position sizing as the base portfolio spec above, with the single change that the NSI Q5 / Quality Q5 exclusion step is skipped entirely -- the composite is scored on the full eligible universe every week, with no names removed pre-scoring.
stripped_base_construction.implementation_note: The live pipeline (paper_trading/signals.py::compute_composite) has exactly one exclusion choke point: `syms = [s for s in syms_today if s not in excluded]` before any signal is scored. The stripped base sets `syms = syms_today` directly at that point and otherwise reuses the same scoring/weighting code.
stripped_base_construction.consequence_disclosed_in_advance: Because percentile ranks (ibs/rsi2/sector_rs) are computed within the surviving universe each week, a stripped-base run will have a different (larger) universe_size and different rank denominators than the live V3.1 run. This is expected and is the entire point of the test -- it is not a bug to reconcile.

test_portfolios.A: Stripped Base -- no exclusions. Benchmark for this test.
test_portfolios.B: Stripped Base + NSI Q5 exclusion only
test_portfolios.C: Stripped Base + Quality Q5 exclusion only
test_portfolios.D: Stripped Base + NSI Q5 + Quality Q5 (= current live V3.1 spec)
test_portfolios.E: Stripped Base + NSI Q5 + Quality Q5 + Accruals Q5 -- SKIPPED. The Sloan accruals formula (strategies/accruals.py) has not passed its 2010-01-31 sanity check even after the healthcare-exclusion fix (Q1 ROA ~0, 34.78% loss-making names per TODO.txt item 4); the profitability floor fix referenced in the task brief has not been implemented. Running Portfolio E on an unvalidated signal would produce an uninterpretable comparison, so it is registered as skipped in advance rather than run and discarded post hoc.

exclusion_definitions.nsi_q5: Net share issuance = (sharesbas_now - sharesbas_1yr_ago) / sharesbas_1yr_ago using MRQ fundamentals. Quintiled ascending (Q5 = heaviest issuers/dilution) among that week's eligible (or stripped-base eligible) universe. Excluded: Q5.
exclusion_definitions.quality_q5: 6-component composite quality score (roe, roa, gm, dte, icr, cfe from strategies/quality.py), each cross-sectionally percentile-ranked and averaged (requires >=4 of 6 non-NaN components, >=5 names). Quintiled descending by score (Q5 = lowest quality). Excluded: Q5.
exclusion_definitions.recompute_frequency: Computed once per calendar month and held for every Friday rebalance within that month -- matches the live pipeline's monthly caching exactly. Not changed for this test.
exclusion_definitions.cutoff_universe_by_portfolio: For B, C, D, the NSI/Quality Q5 cutoffs are computed on that portfolio's own pre-exclusion eligible universe each month (i.e. the same underlying eligible set as Portfolio A, since none of B/C/D's exclusions are sequentially compounding cutoffs -- NSI and Quality are each computed once on the full eligible set, then applied independently or jointly).

return: Excess CAGR over SPY (full-period buy-and-hold CAGR difference)
Factor-adjusted alpha (FF5+UMD, monthly, local factor files -- no network dependency)
downside: Crash-period cumulative returns: 2008-2009 (GFC), 2020-02 to 2020-04 (COVID crash), 2022 calendar year (bear market)
efficiency: Annual modeled cost (10bps round-trip on weekly turnover, annualized)
portfolio: Average position size in dollars (assuming $100,000 total notional per track, matching paper_trading/config.json)
Concentration (HHI of weights -- exactly 1/n each week under equal weighting)

falsification_criteria.valuable: An exclusion is VALUABLE if it improves ANY TWO of: Sharpe ratio by >= 0.05; Max drawdown by >= 2 percentage points (less negative); Left-tail 5th-percentile monthly return by >= 0.5%/month; Factor alpha by >= 0.5%/yr -- each measured relative to Portfolio A (Stripped Base).
falsification_criteria.neutral: An exclusion is NEUTRAL if it improves fewer than two of the above metrics by the stated thresholds.
falsification_criteria.harmful: An exclusion is HARMFUL if it materially worsens more than two metrics: decreases CAGR by > 1%/yr, OR increases max drawdown by > 2 percentage points, relative to Portfolio A.
falsification_criteria.application: Applied independently and literally to B, C, and D (each vs A). No discretion in edge cases -- the thresholds decide the verdict as written.

sub_period_analysis.rationale: These are the periods where downside protection is expected to matter most, per the research background (both exclusion signals' spreads are short-leg-driven).

active_return_orthogonality_platform_fix.purpose: Fixes the platform orthogonality metric flagged in the prior residual-momentum audit, which reported raw return correlation rather than active-return correlation.
reported_for_every_portfolio_A_through_D: Correlation of (portfolio weekly return - SPY weekly return) vs (Portfolio D weekly return - SPY weekly return)
Correlation of monthly FF5+UMD regression residuals vs Portfolio D's residuals, over overlapping months
Holdings Jaccard similarity vs Portfolio D's holdings, averaged over all shared rebalance dates
active_return_orthogonality_platform_fix.note: SPY weekly return is approximated by compounding the local daily total-return series (data/spy_total_return_daily_2001_2024.csv) over each portfolio week's [entry_date, exit_date) window on a close-to-close basis, while portfolio legs are entered/exited at Monday opens. This open-vs-close mismatch is a known, disclosed approximation, not a lookahead violation -- it affects the SPY leg of a correlation calculation, not the portfolio return itself.

development_period.rationale: Full history. This is a portfolio construction audit of an existing, already-registered live specification, not a signal discovery exercise -- no holdout split is applied. Holdout budget for new-signal research is exhausted per project convention; forward validation for this audit is the existing 26-week paper-trading checkpoint on the live V3.1 track, which already runs with both exclusions applied.

constraints: Preregistration is committed (this file, before any portfolio is run) and not edited post-hoc based on results.

Stripped Base must be genuinely V3.1 minus exclusions -- identical signals, weights, universe, rebalance frequency, cost model, and position sizing to the live spec, changed only at the single exclusion choke point.
All test portfolios that are run (A-D; E registered as skipped) are reported in full -- no selective reporting of only the best-looking variant.
Active-return orthogonality is reported for every portfolio.
No new exclusion signals (short interest, momentum decile, etc.) are tested until NSI Q5 and Quality Q5 are fully audited under this preregistration.
No new composite or paper track is built from these results. This is an audit; construction changes, if any, are a separate future decision.
paper_trading/state/ is not read from or written to by this audit -- Tracks 1-3 remain frozen and untouched, per RESEARCH_PLATFORM.md.
deliverables: Full output table, Portfolios A-D (E noted as skipped)
Marginal contribution verdicts (B/C/D vs A) per the falsification criteria above
Honest paragraph: do the existing V3.1 exclusions earn their place, or are they cosmetic?
stop_condition: Report results and wait for instruction. Do not build a new composite or paper track. Do not test additional exclusion signals.
